task: Halfway through a client meeting, someone asks what your role is again. On this project you're looking after the testing. Answer in one sentence.
say: Sorry, what was your role again?
zh: 客户会议进行到一半，有人再问你的职位是什么。你在这个项目里负责测试。用一句话回答。对方说：不好意思，你是负责什么的来着？
example: No worries. My job title's {role}, and on this project I'm looking after the testing.

task: A client asks how long you've worked at your company. It's been about three years. Answer in one or two sentences.
say: How long have you been with your company?
zh: 客户问你在现在的公司工作多久了。大约三年。用一两句话回答。对方说：你在你们公司做了多久了？
example: I've been at {company} about three years now. It's gone really fast!

task: A client asks which team you're in. You're in the cloud team, which looks after hosting and migrations.
say: Which team are you in?
zh: 客户问你在哪个团队。你在云团队，负责托管和迁移。对方说：你在哪个团队？
example: I'm in the cloud team at {company}. We look after hosting and migrations.

task: A client asks where you're based. You work in your company's Auckland office, but you work with clients all over New Zealand.
say: Are you based in Auckland?
zh: 客户问你在哪里办公。你在公司的奥克兰办公室，但客户遍布新西兰各地。对方说：你是在奥克兰工作吗？
example: Yes, I'm in our Auckland office, but I work with clients all over the country.

task: A client checks that you're the person to call when something breaks. You look after support for their systems. Confirm it in one or two sentences.
say: So you're the one who fixes things if they break?
zh: 客户确认出了故障是不是找你。你负责他们系统的技术支持。用一两句话确认。对方说：所以东西坏了就是你来修？
example: Yep, that's me. I look after support for your systems, so if anything breaks, I'm the one to call.

task: A client thinks you're the developer. You're on the testing side; Raj is the developer. Correct them politely and say what you do.
say: Are you the developer?
zh: 客户以为你是开发人员。其实你负责测试，开发是 Raj。礼貌地纠正，并说明你做什么。对方说：你是开发人员吗？
example: No, that's Raj. I'm on the testing side, so I make sure everything works properly before it goes live.

task: A client asks about your background. You started in networking, then moved into cloud about four years ago.
say: What's your background?
zh: 客户问你的背景。你一开始做网络，大约四年前转到了云计算。对方说：你是什么背景？
example: My background's in networking. Then about four years ago I moved into cloud, and that's what I've been doing ever since.

task: A school principal asks if you've worked with schools before. Last year you did two similar projects for other schools.
say: Have you worked with schools before?
zh: 一位校长问你以前有没有和学校合作过。去年你为其他学校做过两个类似的项目。对方说：你以前和学校合作过吗？
example: Yes, I have. Last year I did two similar projects for other schools, so I know how things work in a school environment.

task: A client asks what you'll be working on for them. You'll be setting up backups and monitoring for their servers. Answer in two sentences and say why it's good for them.
say: So what will you be working on for us?
zh: 客户问你要为他们做什么。你将为他们的服务器设置备份和监控。用两句话回答，并说明对他们的好处。对方说：那你会为我们做哪些工作？
example: I'll be setting up backups and monitoring for your servers. So if anything goes wrong, we'll know about it straight away, and your data will be safe.

task: A client asks what a solution architect does. Imagine that's your job title. Explain it in one or two simple sentences.
say: What does a solution architect actually do?
zh: 客户问解决方案架构师是做什么的。假设这就是你的职位。用一两句简单的话解释。对方说：解决方案架构师到底是做什么的？
example: Basically, I design how all the pieces fit together before anyone starts building. A bit like an architect drawing the plans for a house.

task: A client asks if this is your first project like this. It's actually your third Microsoft 365 rollout. Answer confidently.
say: Is this your first project like this?
zh: 客户问这是不是你第一次做这类项目。其实这已经是你第三个 Microsoft 365 部署项目了。自信地回答。对方说：这是你第一次做这类项目吗？
example: No, it's actually my third Microsoft 365 rollout, so I've got a pretty good idea of what to expect.

task: A client asks you about an invoice. You're on the technical side; billing is handled by your account manager, Sarah. Say who looks after it and offer to connect them.
say: Can I ask you about last month's invoice?
zh: 客户问你关于发票的事。你是做技术的，账单由客户经理 Sarah 负责。说明该找谁，并主动帮他们联系。对方说：我能问一下上个月发票的事吗？
example: Ah, that's not really my area. Sarah, our account manager, looks after billing. I'll send her a message now and ask her to give you a call.

task: The client's office manager asks what you actually do. You look after their servers and check that the backups run every night. Explain with no jargon.
say: So what is it you actually do for us?
zh: 客户的办公室经理问你到底是做什么的。你负责他们的服务器，并检查每晚的备份是否成功。不用专业术语来解释。对方说：你到底为我们做些什么？
example: I look after your servers, the big computers that run all your systems. Every night they make a backup copy of your files, and I check it's worked. So if something goes wrong, nothing gets lost.

task: The client's IT manager asks what you'll be handling. You're setting up their Azure landing zone: subscriptions, networking and identity. Answer with the right technical words.
say: So what's your scope on this?
zh: 客户的 IT 经理问你负责哪些工作。你负责搭建他们的 Azure 登陆区：订阅、网络和身份认证。用恰当的技术词汇回答。对方说：那你在这个项目里负责的范围是什么？
example: I'm handling the landing zone, so the subscriptions, networking and identity setup. Basically all the foundations, before we move any workloads across. I'd like to go through your current network design with you early on.

task: A client asks how long you've been doing this. You've been in IT for about seven years, mostly on the data side. Answer confidently, without bragging or underselling.
say: How long have you been doing this kind of work?
zh: 客户问你做这行多久了。你在 IT 行业大约七年，主要做数据方面。自信地回答，既不吹嘘也不过分谦虚。对方说：你做这类工作多久了？
example: About seven years now, mostly on the data side. I've worked on a fair few reporting projects, so I've got a good idea of what works and what doesn't.

task: Over lunch, a client asks where you're from. You moved to New Zealand about six years ago to study IT in Auckland, and you've worked here since. Answer and ask something back.
say: Where are you from originally?
zh: 和客户吃午饭时，对方问你是哪里人。你大约六年前来新西兰，在奥克兰读 IT，之后一直在这里工作。回答，再反问一个问题。对方说：你老家是哪里的？
example: I'm originally from {hometown}. I came over about six years ago to study IT in Auckland, and I've been working here ever since. Have you ever been over that way?

task: A client asks what you bring to the team. Your strength is explaining technical things in plain language. Say it without sounding boastful.
say: So what would you say you bring to the team?
zh: 客户问你能给团队带来什么。你的长处是用通俗的语言解释技术问题。说出来，但别显得在自夸。对方说：你觉得你能给团队带来什么？
example: I'd say my strength is explaining technical stuff in plain English. I'm often the one sitting between the tech team and the business, making sure everyone's on the same page.

task: After your five-second intro, a client asks what you do exactly. On this project you're bringing all their sales data into one place. Right now it's spread across four systems.
say: So what do you do exactly?
zh: 你做完五秒钟的介绍后，客户问你具体做什么。在这个项目里，你要把他们所有的销售数据集中到一个地方。现在这些数据分散在四个系统里。对方说：那你具体是做什么的？
example: On this project, I'm bringing all your sales data into one place. At the moment it's spread across four different systems, so once it's together, you'll be able to report on it properly.

task: A client asks if you only work on their project. You're on their project Monday to Wednesday and with other clients the rest of the week. Explain and say how they can reach you.
say: Do you work with other clients as well?
zh: 客户问你是不是只做他们的项目。你周一到周三做他们的项目，其余时间做其他客户。解释一下，并告诉他们怎么联系你。对方说：你还同时做别的客户吗？
example: I do, yes. I'm on your project Monday to Wednesday, and with other clients the rest of the week. But if you need me on a Thursday or Friday, just send me a message.

task: A client asks if you also handle security. You don't; your colleague Raj in the security team does. Say so and offer to bring him in.
say: Do you look after the security side too?
zh: 客户问你是否也负责安全方面。你不负责，安全团队的同事 Raj 负责。说明这一点，并提出让他参与进来。对方说：安全方面也是你负责吗？
example: Not me, no. That's Raj in our security team, and he's really good. I'll invite him to our next meeting so you can ask him directly.

task: A client asks what you did before your current job. You worked on the IT help desk at a bank for about three years. Answer and add one thing you learned.
say: What were you doing before this job?
zh: 客户问你做现在这份工作之前在做什么。你在一家银行的 IT 服务台工作了大约三年。回答，并加一点你学到的东西。对方说：你做这份工作之前在做什么？
example: I was on the IT help desk at a bank for about three years. It was a great place to start. You learn very quickly how to stay calm when people are stressed!

task: A senior client exec asks for your role in one sentence. You're making sure their new finance system goes live on time without disrupting month-end.
say: In one sentence, what's your role on this?
zh: 一位客户高管要你用一句话说明你的角色。你负责确保他们的新财务系统按时上线，并且不影响月末结账。对方说：用一句话说，你在这个项目里是什么角色？
example: I'm making sure your new finance system goes live on time, without getting in the way of month-end.

task: A client asks why you were chosen for their project. You've done four similar data migrations, and you're known for careful testing. Mention your strengths without bragging.
say: Why did they put you on our project?
zh: 客户问为什么选你来做他们的项目。你做过四个类似的数据迁移，而且以测试仔细出名。说出你的长处，但不要吹嘘。对方说：他们为什么派你来做我们的项目？
example: I think it's because I've done four similar data migrations, so I know where the problems usually hide. I'm also pretty fussy about testing, which is a good thing on a project like this.

task: A client asks if you're fairly new. You've been in IT for two years, but you've already delivered three rollouts like this one, and you have senior colleagues to call on. Answer confidently, without getting defensive.
say: Are you fairly new to this?
zh: 客户问你是不是新手。你在 IT 行业两年，但已经完成过三个类似的部署项目，而且有资深同事可以请教。自信地回答，不要显得防备。对方说：你做这行时间不长吧？
example: Fairly new, yes. I've been in IT for two years, but I've already delivered three rollouts like this one. And if anything unusual comes up, I've got some very experienced colleagues I can call on.

task: A client asks if you've done this kind of project before. You've never used this exact CRM, but you've done two CRM rollouts on another platform. Be honest and still sound confident.
say: Have you done this kind of project before?
zh: 客户问你以前有没有做过这类项目。你没用过这个具体的 CRM，但在另一个平台上做过两次 CRM 部署。诚实回答，同时显得有信心。对方说：你以前做过这类项目吗？
example: Not with this exact CRM, to be honest. But I've done two CRM rollouts on another platform, and the hard parts are usually the same: cleaning up the data and getting people to use it. The product itself, I'll pick up quickly.

task: The client's IT manager asks how you'll work together day to day. There's a stand-up every morning at 9:15, you'll post notes in the project Teams channel, and you'll work alongside their sysadmin, Mike.
say: How will we work together day to day?
zh: 客户的 IT 经理问你们日常怎么合作。每天早上 9:15 有站会，你会在项目的 Teams 频道里发笔记，并和他们的系统管理员 Mike 一起工作。对方说：我们日常怎么配合？
example: We'll have a quick stand-up every morning at 9:15. I'll post notes and updates in the project Teams channel. And I'll be working side by side with Mike, so he'll know everything I'm doing.

task: A client asks what brought you to New Zealand. You came about eight years ago to do a Master's in IT, then got a job and stayed. Answer briefly and positively, then bring it back to work.
say: So what brought you to New Zealand?
zh: 客户问你为什么来新西兰。大约八年前你来读 IT 硕士，后来找到工作就留下了。简短积极地回答，再把话题带回工作。对方说：你当初为什么来新西兰？
example: I came over about eight years ago to do a Master's in IT, then I got a job and just stayed. I love it here. It's been a great place to build a career in tech.

task: A client is confused about what you and your colleague Aroha each do. Aroha handles the planning and budget; you handle the technical design and build. Explain who to go to for what.
say: What's the difference between you and Aroha?
zh: 客户搞不清你和同事 Aroha 各自负责什么。Aroha 负责计划和预算，你负责技术设计和搭建。说明什么事该找谁。对方说：你和 Aroha 有什么区别？
example: Good question. Aroha looks after the planning and the budget, so timelines and costs go to her. I look after the technical design and the build. If it's about how something works, come to me.

task: A client thinks you're running the staff training. You're not: their own HR team will run it, using training materials you're writing. Explain and offer some help.
say: So you'll be training our staff, right?
zh: 客户以为员工培训由你来做。其实不是：培训由他们自己的 HR 团队负责，用的是你写的培训材料。解释清楚，并主动提供一些帮助。对方说：所以员工培训是你来做，对吧？
example: Not quite. Your HR team will run the training, because they know your people best. My job is writing the training materials and making sure they're easy to follow. I'm happy to help them prepare, though.

task: At a pre-sales meeting, a client asks about your experience in healthcare. You spent two years supporting a regional hospital's systems as part of a managed service. Don't name the hospital.
say: Tell us a bit about your experience in healthcare.
zh: 在售前会议上，客户问你在医疗行业的经验。你曾在一项托管服务中为一家地区医院提供了两年的系统支持。不要说出医院的名字。对方说：介绍一下你在医疗行业的经验吧。
example: Sure. For two years I supported the systems at a regional hospital, as part of a managed service. So I understand how important it is that things stay up, and that changes are planned really carefully.

task: Imagine your job title is DevOps engineer. A non-technical client exec doesn't see why they need one. Explain the value in plain language: you help their developers release updates faster and more safely.
say: Honestly, I've no idea what a DevOps engineer does. Why do we need one?
zh: 假设你的职位是 DevOps 工程师。一位不懂技术的客户高管不明白为什么需要这个职位。用通俗的语言说明价值：你帮他们的开发人员更快、更安全地发布更新。对方说：说实话，我完全不知道 DevOps 工程师是做什么的。我们为什么需要？
example: Fair question! Your developers write the code, and I build the tools that get it out to your customers quickly and safely. So instead of a big, risky update every few months, you can release small changes every week, with much less chance of something breaking.

task: A client suggests you might not understand how things work in New Zealand. You've lived and worked here for five years, including projects with two local councils. Answer calmly and confidently, without sounding defensive.
say: You seem fairly new to New Zealand. Do you understand how things work here?
zh: 客户暗示你可能不了解新西兰的做事方式。你在这里生活工作了五年，还和两个地方政府做过项目。冷静、自信地回答，不要显得防备。对方说：你好像来新西兰不久。你了解这里的做事方式吗？
example: I can see why you'd ask. I've actually been here about five years, and I've worked with two local councils in that time, so I know how things are done here. And coming from somewhere else, I sometimes spot things others miss.

task: While you're on site, a client asks you to fix their phone system. Phones are managed by a different supplier. Say no politely, say who looks after it, and offer something helpful.
say: While you're here, can you sort out our phones too?
zh: 你在客户现场时，客户请你顺便修一下电话系统。电话是另一家供应商管理的。礼貌地拒绝，说明该找谁，并提供一些力所能及的帮助。对方说：你既然来了，能不能顺便把我们的电话也弄一下？
example: I wish I could! But your phones are managed by a different supplier, so I'd only make things worse. What I can do is find their support number for you, and if they need any network details from us, I'm happy to help.

task: A client mistakes you for a salesperson. You're on the technical side; Sarah is the account manager. Your job is to make sure what they already have works well. Answer with a light touch.
say: So you're the one trying to sell us more licences?
zh: 客户把你当成了销售。你是做技术的，客户经理是 Sarah。你的工作是确保他们已有的东西运作良好。轻松地回答。对方说：所以你是来推销更多许可证的？
example: Ha, no, I'm not here to sell you anything! That's Sarah, our account manager. I'm on the technical side. My job is to make sure what you've already got works well, and if you don't need something, I'll tell you.

task: A senior client manager asks what value you add, because their IT team could do the work. Your team has done this migration about twenty times; their IT team knows their business best. Answer respectfully.
say: Honestly, why do we need you? Our IT team could do this.
zh: 一位客户高级经理问你们能带来什么价值，因为他们的 IT 团队也能做。你们团队做过这种迁移大约二十次，而他们的 IT 团队最了解自己的业务。尊重地回答。对方说：说实话，我们为什么需要你们？我们的 IT 团队也能做。
example: That's a fair point, and your IT team is great. They know your business far better than we do. What we bring is that we've done this exact migration about twenty times, so we know where it goes wrong. Together, it'll be quicker and less risky.

task: The client's finance manager asks how you ended up in IT. You studied accounting, then moved into data analytics about six years ago. Link your background to why you understand finance teams.
say: So how did you end up in IT?
zh: 客户的财务经理问你是怎么进入 IT 行业的。你本科学会计，大约六年前转做数据分析。把你的背景和你为什么了解财务团队联系起来。对方说：你是怎么进入 IT 这行的？
example: I actually studied accounting first. Then about six years ago I moved into data analytics, and I've never looked back. But it means I speak finance, so I know what month-end feels like for your team.

task: A client exec asks you to walk them through your career in a minute. You started on a help desk, moved into systems admin, and now lead cloud projects: about ten years in total. End by linking it to their project.
say: Walk me through your career. You've got a minute.
zh: 一位客户高管请你用一分钟讲讲你的职业经历。你从服务台做起，后来做系统管理，现在带领云项目，总共大约十年。最后把它和他们的项目联系起来。对方说：讲讲你的职业经历吧。给你一分钟。
example: Sure. I started out on the help desk, which taught me a lot about people. Then I moved into systems admin and spent a few years running servers. These days I lead cloud projects. So, about ten years in total. That mix means I get both the tech and the people side, which is exactly what your project needs.

task: A client manager says your team caused yesterday's internet outage. In fact their internet provider had a fault. Your team manages their servers and the network inside the office. Explain your role and what happened without blaming anyone, and offer to look into a backup connection.
say: Your team's in charge of our network, so why did the internet go down yesterday?
zh: 客户经理说昨天的断网是你们团队造成的。其实是他们的网络服务商出了故障。你们团队负责他们的服务器和办公室内部网络。解释你们的职责和事情经过，不要指责任何人，并提出研究一下备用线路。对方说：你们负责我们的网络，那昨天为什么断网了？
example: I understand the frustration. Just to be clear on roles, we look after your servers and the network inside the office. The internet connection itself comes from your provider, and yesterday they had a fault on their side. That said, I'll look into a backup connection, so it doesn't hit you this hard again.

task: The client's CFO and IT team are both in the room and ask about your role. You're building a new data platform. Explain it once for finance (faster, more reliable reports) and once for IT (data pipelines into a cloud data warehouse).
say: Can you explain your role in a way that works for all of us?
zh: 客户的财务总监和 IT 团队都在场，问你的角色是什么。你在搭建新的数据平台。先对财务的人讲一遍（报表更快、更可靠），再对 IT 的人讲一遍（把数据管道接入云数据仓库）。对方说：你能用我们都听得懂的方式解释一下你的角色吗？
example: Sure. For the finance folks: I'm making your reports faster and more reliable, so you're not waiting on spreadsheets. For the IT team: I'm building the data pipelines from your core systems into a cloud data warehouse. Same project, two angles. Happy to go deeper with either group afterwards.

task: A client asks what you're NOT responsible for. You cover the migration and the first month of support. End-user training is their IT team's job, and licence purchasing goes through Sarah, your account manager. Be clear, and promise to flag gaps early.
say: What are you not doing for us? I want to know where the gaps are.
zh: 客户问哪些事不归你负责。你负责迁移和上线后第一个月的支持。最终用户培训由他们的 IT 团队负责，购买许可证要通过你们的客户经理 Sarah。说清楚，并承诺发现遗漏会尽早提出。对方说：哪些事你们不做？我想知道有哪些空白。
example: Good question. I'm covering the migration itself and the first month of support after go-live. I'm not doing end-user training, that's your IT team, and licence purchasing goes through Sarah, our account manager. If anything else comes up that isn't covered, I'll flag it early.
